claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a single-phase, relatively uniform, disordered solid solution.
Heating HfNbTaTiZr to 600–900°C activates dynamic local lattice distortions.
Dynamic lattice distortions promote transient short-range chemical ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated atomic vibrations enhance local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions transiently reorganize chemical species into short-range order.
Transient ordering decreases local bonding uniformity and alters interatomic bonding.
The proposed structural evolution reduces effective barriers for dislocation motion and changes dislocation mobility.
HfNbTaTiZr will show an altered elevated-temperature stress–strain response relative to room temperature.
The altered stress–strain response may include slight stress drops or changes in yielding behavior.
The thermal expansion coefficient will increase nonlinearly between 600°C and 900°C relative to the room-temperature baseline.
The elastic modulus will measurably decrease or soften between 600°C and 900°C.
Elevated-temperature diffraction will show peak broadening or subtle peak splitting caused by transient ordering.
At room temperature, dynamic lattice distortions and chemical ordering are minimal.
The proposed effects are most pronounced between 600°C and 900°C under low-strain-rate elastic and early-plastic deformation.
Outside 600–900°C or under different strain conditions, signatures of dynamic distortions and ordering will diminish or change character.
In situ neutron diffraction and resonant ultrasound spectroscopy can be used to determine elastic moduli in refractory high-entropy alloys.
In situ neutron experiments can compare elastic and plastic deformation at room and elevated temperatures in a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed mechanism is falsified if all measured macroscopic responses show no significant elevated-temperature deviation and simulations show neither increased distortion nor transient ordering.
